user_story: As a visitor, I want the home page to explain the board and send me to the jobs so I can start from a short introduction.
expected_behavior: The home page h1 is “The board for endpoint engineers.” | The lead says daily listings for macOS, Windows, MDM, and endpoint security roles. | “See the jobs” links to /board. | The page revalidates every 3600 seconds and is indexable.
notes: Home is a landing page. The job board is /board.

user_story: As a visitor, I want the home page to show how many roles are open, remote or hybrid, and salary-disclosed so I can judge the board before opening it.
expected_behavior: Three stats render: Open roles, Remote or hybrid, and Salary shown. | Open roles is the deduped filtered total for the default filters. | Remote or hybrid counts jobs whose resolved workplace is Remote or Hybrid. | Salary shown counts jobs that have a salary. | Counts use en-US grouping. | An empty feed still renders the stats at 0.
notes: The home HTML size check requires the text “Remote or hybrid”.

user_story: As a visitor, I want a short list of the newest open roles so I can open one without loading the full board.
expected_behavior: The preview is labelled “Newest open roles” and lists at most four jobs from page 1 of the default newest sort. | Each row links to /jobs/{id} and shows title, company, and resolved workplace. | “All roles” links to /board. | When the active feed is empty the preview says “No open roles yet.”

user_story: As a visitor, I want the home page to say what an account is for so I know whether signing in is worth it.
expected_behavior: The section says an account is optional and that Google or GitHub sign-in keeps saved jobs, filters the user chooses to keep, and which listings they have opened. | It links to /privacy. | Signing in does not save filters, saved jobs, or opened listings, because no application code writes user_preferences, saved_jobs, or job_views.
notes: The copy is on the page. The three account capabilities it names are not wired. See ACCT-01, ACCT-02, and ACCT-03.

user_story: As a visitor with an old home-page filter link, I want it to open the board with the same query so bookmarks keep working.
expected_behavior: A request to / with q, location, platforms, tools, metroAreas, workplace, sponsorship, salary, leadership, minSalary, seniority, family, freshness, sort, locations, remote, or page redirects 308 to the same query on /board. | / with no board query stays on the landing page. | Other paths are not redirected.

user_story: As a search engine, I want the home page to describe the site so the landing URL is not treated as the job list.
expected_behavior: Home emits JSON-LD for WebSite, Organization, SoftwareApplication, and a breadcrumb. | It does not emit the job collection graph. | The collection graph is emitted on /board from the active feed’s first 20 jobs.

user_story: As a job seeker, I want /board to open on current endpoint listings so I can search without a separate data service.
expected_behavior: /board renders JobBoard from the active jobs in src/data/jobs.json. | The first page is computed on the server for the default filters. | Later filter and page changes load /api/board. | The page title is “Job board”, the canonical URL is /board, and the page is indexable. | The board revalidates every 3600 seconds.

user_story: As a job seeker, I want coverage numbers for the current result set so I can see how many roles are mapped, remote or hybrid, and salary-disclosed.
expected_behavior: The rail’s tracked-role count stays the deduped size of the active feed. | Current view, Mapped, Remote / hybrid, and Salary shown recompute from the filtered visible jobs. | Meter widths are rounded percentages of the current view, and they are 0 when that view is empty. | The tracked count is aria-hidden as a number and also exposed as “{n} tracked roles”.

user_story: As a mobile visitor, I want the coverage numbers behind a disclosure so the first screen stays on search and results.
expected_behavior: Below the results, a details element labelled “Coverage stats” contains the same coverage rail. | It is closed until the visitor opens it.
notes: The desktop rail and this disclosure both render. Responsive CSS hides the desktop rail at narrow widths.

user_story: As a job seeker, I want the result heading to show how many roles match so I know the size of the current search.
expected_behavior: The results region is labelled “Job listings” and its heading reads “{total} endpoint opportunities”. | The number is also in screen-reader text because the animated number is aria-hidden. | A “Daily refresh” note sits beside the result sort control. | The region is aria-busy while a board query is loading, and a visually hidden “Loading results” message is present.

user_story: As a job seeker, I want a failed result refresh to keep the last results and let me try again so a network error does not wipe the board.
expected_behavior: Keyword and location edits wait 200ms before the board query. Other filter changes query immediately. | GET /api/board returns the filtered page with Cache-Control public, max-age=0, s-maxage=3600, stale-while-revalidate=86400. | A non-OK response or an unexpected payload sets an alert “Results did not refresh.” with a Try again button. | Try again repeats the same query. | The initial server page is shown until the first client query replaces it.

user_story: As a job seeker, I want to search words such as Jamf or Intune so only listings that contain them remain.
expected_behavior: The search box is labelled “Search jobs”, named q, and uses placeholder “Search Jamf, Intune, macOS, Kandji/Iru...”. | A trimmed query matches title, company, location, summary, description, seniority, employment type, tags, tools, and platforms, case-insensitively. | A blank query does not filter. | A polite live region announces “{n} role found” or “{n} roles found”.

user_story: As a keyboard user, I want / to focus search so I can start typing without tabbing through the page.
expected_behavior: Pressing / focuses #job-search-input and prevents the character from being typed elsewhere. | The shortcut does nothing when the key event target is an input, textarea, select, or contenteditable element, or when Meta, Ctrl, or Alt is held.

user_story: As a job seeker, I want matches highlighted and a way to clear the query so I can see why a card matched and start over.
expected_behavior: Queries of at least two characters wrap case-insensitive matches in mark.search-hit inside the title, company, and summary. | One-character queries are not highlighted. | The highlight pattern escapes regex characters. | When a query is present, “Clear job search” empties it and returns focus to the search box.

user_story: As a job seeker, I want to type a city, state, or country so I can narrow listings geographically.
expected_behavior: The location field is labelled “Search locations” and placeholder “City, state, or country”. | A folded query matches the job location, the mapped location label, and the resolved workplace text. | A blank value does not filter. | The value is stored as the location query parameter.

user_story: As a job seeker, I want Remote, Hybrid, and On-site as separate choices so workplace is not mixed into the text search.
expected_behavior: The workplace group offers Any, Remote, Hybrid, and On-site, each with a deduped role count. | Selecting one keeps jobs whose resolved workplace equals that value. | Counts are computed before the workplace filter, so they stay visible after a workplace is chosen. | Copy that explicitly says the role is not remote or hybrid, or an Indeed in-person work location, resolves to On-site even when the stored workplace is Remote or Hybrid. | A stored On-site value stays On-site.

user_story: As a job seeker, I want to keep only roles that disclose pay so I can skip listings with no salary.
expected_behavior: The Salary shown toggle is aria-pressed. | When it is on, a job remains only if salary.min or salary.max is a number. | The active chip is “Salary shown” and removing it turns the toggle off. | The URL parameter is salary=1.

user_story: As a job seeker, I want a leadership filter so I can focus on management and technical-lead titles.
expected_behavior: The Leadership toggle is aria-pressed and uses leadership=1. | A title matches when it contains a whole-word executive term, a whole-word lead, or manager without the excluded product, account, and tool-manager phrases. | It composes with the exact seniority filter. | The chip label is “Leadership”.

user_story: As a job seeker, I want to filter by role family so I can stay inside endpoint engineering, security, platform, or automation work.
expected_behavior: The Role select offers All plus Endpoint Engineering, macOS Platform, Windows Platform, Workplace Systems, Endpoint Security, Device Compliance, Systems Administration, and Automation. | All clears the filter. | Any other value keeps jobs whose roleFamily is exactly that value. | The URL parameter is family.

user_story: As a job seeker, I want to limit results to recently posted roles so older listings drop out.
expected_behavior: Freshness offers Any, Last 1 day, Last 7 days, Last 14 days, and Last 30 days. | A window keeps a job only when the posted date is known and postedAt is inside that many days. | Jobs whose posted date equals fetchedAt and have no source age evidence are “Date unknown” and fail every window. | The URL parameter is freshness.
notes: This is the posting-age filter. The feed’s Updated timestamp is FRESH-01.

user_story: As a job seeker, I want to select macOS, Windows, iOS, Android, or Linux so I can focus on my platform.
expected_behavior: Each platform is an aria-pressed toggle. | One or more selected platforms keep a job when any of its platforms is selected. | Each selected platform has its own removable chip. | The URL parameter is a comma-separated platforms list.

user_story: As a job seeker, I want to filter by Jamf, Intune, SCCM, and the other endpoint tools so I can target my stack.
expected_behavior: Tool toggles cover Jamf, Intune, SCCM, Fleet MDM, Kandji, NinjaOne, Workspace ONE, Tanium, Okta, Google Workspace, Entra ID, Autopilot, PowerShell, and Defender. | A job matches when it includes any selected tool. | Each selected tool has a removable chip. | The URL parameter is a comma-separated tools list, except a single tool is carried by the path in FILT-14.

user_story: As a job seeker, I want metro-area choices so I can narrow listings to a city or region without guessing spellings.
expected_behavior: Metro choices come from metroAreaOptions, including US metros and European and Latin American metros such as London, Berlin, Munich, Madrid, Zurich, Mexico City, and São Paulo. | A job matches when any selected metro’s matcher accepts its location text, including known aliases. | Chips are labelled “Metro: {name}”. | The URL parameter is metroAreas, with values separated by | because names contain commas.

user_story: As a job seeker, I want to filter by seniority so the level matches the role I want.
expected_behavior: Seniority offers All, Associate, Mid, Senior, Staff, Lead, and Manager. | All clears the filter. | Any other value keeps jobs whose seniority field equals it. | The URL parameter is seniority.

user_story: As a job seeker, I want to filter by the sponsorship statement so I can separate available, case-by-case, unavailable, and unstated listings.
expected_behavior: The Visa sponsorship select offers Any, Available, Case-by-case, Unavailable, and Not stated. | A selected status matches visaSponsorship.status, and a missing status is treated as not-stated. | Remote does not imply sponsorship. | The chip reads “Visa: {label}”. | The URL parameter is sponsorship.

user_story: As a job seeker, I want a salary floor so I can hide roles whose disclosed range cannot reach it.
expected_behavior: The control offers Any salary, $80k+, $100k+, $120k+, $150k+, $180k+, and $200k+. | A floor keeps a job only when salary.currency is USD and salary.max, or salary.min when max is absent, is at least that amount. | Non-USD and missing salaries are excluded. | The chip is “Minimum: {label}”. | The URL parameter is minSalary.
notes: The floor uses the stored currency before location-based display conversion. A displayed non-USD salary still fails a USD floor.

user_story: As a job seeker, I want each active filter visible and removable so I can tell why the results changed.
expected_behavior: Every non-default query, location, workplace, salary, leadership, minimum salary, role, freshness, seniority, sort, sponsorship, platform, tool, and metro produces a chip. | Each chip’s accessible name is “Remove filter: {label}”. | Clear all restores the initial filter state. | The sticky region is labelled “Active filters” and is hidden when nothing is active.

user_story: As a job seeker, I want the current filters in the address bar so I can reload or share a search.
expected_behavior: Filters serialize to q, location, platforms, tools, metroAreas, workplace, sponsorship, salary, leadership, minSalary, seniority, family, freshness, and sort. | Default values are omitted. | A single selected tool moves the path to /{tool-slug} and still records tools in the query when the board API is called. | Two or more tools, or none, use /board. | Same-path updates use history.replaceState. A path change uses the Next router with scroll false. | The board page number is not written into this URL.
notes: Signed-in filter restore is ACCT-01. This story is the address bar only.

user_story: As a browser user, I want Back and Forward to restore the filter URL so history matches what I see.
expected_behavior: The filter store listens for popstate and for its own filter-change event. | After a history traversal, filters are read again from the pathname and query. | Invalid enum values fall back to Any, All, or newest. | Unknown platform, tool, and metro tokens are dropped.

user_story: As a job seeker arriving from search, I want a page per endpoint tool so that tool is already selected.
expected_behavior: Each endpoint tool has a static path such as /jamf or /intune. | The page opens the board with that tool selected. | Unknown slugs are not generated and call notFound. | dynamicParams is false, so static routes such as /board, /jobs, /privacy, /api, and /api-docs win over this segment. | Metadata title, description, canonical URL, Open Graph, and Twitter cards come from getEndpointToolSeo.

user_story: As a visitor with an older filter link, I want remote=1 to still mean Remote and obsolete parameters to be dropped on the next update.
expected_behavior: remote=1 with no workplace parameter is read as workplace Remote. | An explicit workplace value wins. | locations and remote are deleted the next time filters are written to the URL. | Unknown query keys are ignored by the board parser.

user_story: As a job seeker, I want the less common filters grouped so the first controls stay on role, location, workplace, and platform.
expected_behavior: Visa sponsorship, minimum salary, seniority, sort, metro areas, and tools sit in a details element labelled “Advanced filters”. | It starts closed when none of those are active, and it opens when any of them is active. | The summary shows “{n} active” or “Optional”. | The summary is available at desktop and mobile widths.
notes: There is no separate desktop-only filter stack. The same disclosure is used at every width.

user_story: As a job seeker, I want to ask for a missing city or region so the board can add coverage.
expected_behavior: The link “Don’t see your city or region? Let us know on GitHub.” opens a new GitHub issue URL with a title and body prompts for city, state or province, country, context, and sources. | rel is noopener noreferrer. | The accessible name says it opens in a new tab.

user_story: As a job seeker, I want to sort by newest, compensation, or company so I can scan in the order I need.
expected_behavior: Sort controls in the advanced filters and in the results heading offer Newest, Compensation, and Company. | Newest puts jobs with a known posted date first, then postedAt descending. | Compensation sorts by salary.max, then salary.min, then 0, descending. | Company sorts by company name ascending with localeCompare. | Changing sort returns to page 1. | Non-default sorts chip as “Sort: {label}” and use the sort query parameter.

user_story: As a job seeker, I want long result sets split into pages so the board stays usable.
expected_behavior: The board page size is 20. | Top and bottom controls appear only when there is more than one page. | They show “Showing {start}-{end} of {total}”. | Previous is disabled on page 1 and Next is disabled on the last page. | Number buttons include the ends and the pages around the current page, with an ellipsis for gaps, and the current page is aria-current. | Choosing a page scrolls the results into view, smoothly unless prefers-reduced-motion is set. | A filter change returns to page 1. | The page number is sent to /api/board and is not stored in the shareable filter URL.

user_story: As a job seeker or crawler, I want a paged directory of every active role so I can browse or index them without the interactive filters.
expected_behavior: /jobs lists canonical active jobs, 50 per page, with title, company, location, and a UTC posted date linking to /jobs/{id}. | Page 1 is /jobs. Later pages are /jobs?page={n} and use aria-current on the current page. | A non-positive or non-integer page is treated as page 1. | A page past the last page calls notFound. | Page 1 stays valid when there are no jobs. | Titles and canonical URLs include the page number after page 1.
notes: The directory uses formatPostedDate, so an unknown posted date can read “Fresh” rather than “Date unknown”.

user_story: As a job seeker, I want a disclosed salary shown on the card, the detail page, the comparison, and the map so I do not have to open the source to see it.
expected_behavior: A card with a salary shows an accessible “Salary {label}” pill and a currency symbol from the ISO code. | A card without a salary omits the row. | The job detail sidebar adds a Salary row only when a salary exists. | Comparison shows the salary label or “Not shown”. | Map popups show the salary label or “Salary not listed”.

user_story: As a job seeker outside the US, I want a bare dollar amount in a non-US location shown in that location’s currency so the figure is not presented as USD by default.
expected_behavior: presentSalary changes a USD amount to a location currency only when the salary is not marked as coming from the source and the label has no explicit currency marker. | Recognized locations include the UK, euro-area countries, Switzerland, Canada, Australia, New Zealand, India, Singapore, Mexico, Brazil, Poland, Sweden, and Japan. | A US-context location is left unchanged. | The symbol comes from Intl for a three-letter code and otherwise the code is shown as-is. | The minimum-salary filter still requires the stored currency to be USD.

user_story: As a job seeker, I want the map to stay closed until I ask for it so the listing search does not load the map library first.
expected_behavior: The section is labelled “Mapped job locations”. | It starts collapsed and the button reads “Show map” with aria-expanded false. | Activating it loads map data from /api/board/map and then the MapLibre canvas, which is not server-rendered. | The button then reads “Hide map” and aria-expanded true. | Hiding it unmounts the canvas.

user_story: As a job seeker, I want one point per mapped role and a count of how many roles have coordinates so I know what the map covers.
expected_behavior: The heading shows “{n} mapped jobs” and a pill shows “{n} of {total}” for the current filtered set. | Jobs without mapLocation are skipped. | Jobs that share coordinates remain separate points. | Ambiguous multi-location rows are not given coordinates during refresh.

user_story: As a map user, I want zoom and fit controls so I can inspect a cluster or return to every point.
expected_behavior: The control group is labelled “Map zoom controls” and contains “Zoom in map”, “Zoom out map”, and “Fit map to jobs”. | Zoom stays between 0 and 18. | The buttons disable at those bounds. | A percentage readout follows the current zoom. | Fit uses the configured padding.

user_story: As a job seeker, I want a map point or cluster to show the role, company, salary, and apply link so I can act without leaving the map.
expected_behavior: A point popup shows title, company, salary label or “Salary not listed”, and an Apply link when applyUrl exists. | Apply uses rel noopener noreferrer and target _blank. | A cluster loads at most six jobs and says “Showing {shown} of {count}” when more remain. | On coarse pointers the desktop popup is hidden and a bottom sheet with “Close selected job” is used instead.

user_story: As a map user, I want a failed map load to be recoverable and the basemap to credit its sources.
expected_behavior: While points are loading, the map shows its loading state. | If the map request fails and there are no points, an alert says “Map data did not load.” and Try again refetches. | The dark raster style attributes OpenStreetMap and CARTO. | Reduced-motion and short landscape layouts are covered by the map CSS.

user_story: As a job seeker, I want each card to show the source, date, title, company, workplace, summary, location, age, family, seniority, and employment type so I can scan a role.
expected_behavior: The card shows the source pill, posted label, title link to /jobs/{id}, company, resolved workplace, summary, location, freshness label, role family, seniority, and employment type. | A known posted date uses a time element. An unknown date is the text “Date unknown” without a time element. | The attribution label is shown. | The card id is job-{id}.

user_story: As a job seeker, I want Apply to open the employer listing in a new tab, and a listing with no apply URL to be marked as not applicable.
expected_behavior: When applyUrl is present, Apply opens it with rel noopener noreferrer and target _blank. | When applyUrl is absent, the card shows a non-link “Seed listing” state. | The detail page is different: its apply link uses applyUrl when present and otherwise sourceUrl.

user_story: As a job seeker, I want a durable page for one role so I can read it and share the URL.
expected_behavior: An active canonical job at /jobs/{id} shows source, language when detected, freshness, title, company, summary, location, workplace, employment, seniority, posted date, salary when present, description when it adds detail, and “Apply for this role”. | Apply uses applyUrl or, if that is missing, sourceUrl, with rel noopener noreferrer and target _blank. | Metadata title is “{title} at {company}”, the description is capped near 155 characters, and Open Graph and Twitter cards use the shared image. | The page revalidates every 3600 seconds.

feature: Canonical job URL and missing job
user_story: As a job seeker or crawler, I want duplicate listings to land on one URL and unknown listings to 404 so I do not keep an expired or duplicate page.
expected_behavior: generateStaticParams emits only canonical active ids. | A duplicate id permanently redirects to the canonical id. | An unknown or inactive id calls notFound and its metadata title is “Job not found” with noindex. | The server HTML for a real job includes the title and does not include the old “Loading endpoint roles” text.
notes: There is no custom not-found page. Next.js supplies the 404.

user_story: As a job seeker, I want a longer description when the source has one so I can read it without losing the summary.
expected_behavior: “More description” appears when the listing has a description, extra description blocks, match reasons, platforms, or tools. | Opening it fetches GET /api/board/listings/{id} when the description was omitted from the card payload. | The response is the description text, or 404 “Listing not found” with no-store when the id is absent. | A failed load says “Description did not load.” and offers Try again. | The detail page renders the description inline when the blocks add material beyond the summary.

user_story: As a job seeker, I want the reason a role is on this board and the detected tools so I can judge fit quickly.
expected_behavior: Inside an expanded card, up to three match reasons show immediately and the rest sit behind “View {n} more”. | Compact chips show platforms first, then tools, up to eight, with a “+{n} technologies” remainder. | The list is labelled “Matched tools and platforms”. | A card with no reasons omits the reason block.

user_story: As a job seeker, I want the listing’s sponsorship statement, and a clear “not stated” on the detail page, so I do not infer eligibility from remote work.
expected_behavior: A card hides sponsorship when it is missing or not-stated. | Available, case-by-case, and unavailable render a disclosure with the status label, the evidence quote, and an http(s) source link. | The detail page always shows the disclosure, and uses “Visa sponsorship: Not stated” when nothing was classified. | The note says to confirm conditions with the employer.

user_story: As a job seeker, I want the detail page to show why the role was included and where it was retrieved so I can check the source.
expected_behavior: “Why this role is here” lists every match reason, the source name, the attribution label, the retrieved time, a “View source listing” link for an http(s) source URL, and grouped platform and tool chips. | A non-http source URL is not linked.

user_story: As a job seeker, I want to compare a few roles side by side so I can weigh pay, location, and tools without flipping cards.
expected_behavior: Each card has an aria-pressed Compare button. | One selected role shows “1 role selected” and “Select one more role to compare.” with Clear. | Two to four roles show a table of employer, salary, location, workplace, seniority, tools, match signals, freshness, and apply link. | A fifth role stays disabled until one is removed. | Remove and Clear comparison update the selection. | The selection is kept in memory while filters change and is not saved to the account or the URL. | The table scrolls inside a keyboard region when it overflows.
notes: Saving a comparison is not a saved-jobs feature. Saved jobs are ACCT-03.

user_story: As a job seeker, I want a language label when the listing is not English so I know before I open it.
expected_behavior: A language pill appears only when title and description score at least 2 for Spanish, French, German, Italian, Portuguese, or Dutch rules. | English listings have no language pill. | The same label is shown on the card and the detail page.

user_story: As a job seeker on a role page, I want the breadcrumb and back link to return me to the open roles so I can keep browsing.
expected_behavior: The job page breadcrumb “All endpoint jobs” and the “Browse all roles” link both point at /#open-roles. | The API docs “Browse jobs” link also points at /#open-roles. | The element id open-roles exists on /board and does not exist on the home page, so those links open the landing page and do not scroll to the board.
notes: The footer Job board link correctly goes to /board. These three links were not updated when the board moved off the home page.

user_story: As a visitor, I want to see when the feed was updated so I can judge whether the board is current.
expected_behavior: The top bar and footer format feed.updatedAt in UTC with a short month, day, hour, minute, and time-zone name. | An invalid timestamp reads “Pending refresh”. | The same formatter is used for a job’s retrieved time on the detail page.

user_story: As a job seeker, I want each listing to say when it was posted, or that the date is unknown, so I do not treat a fetch time as a post date.
expected_behavior: A posted date that differs from fetchedAt, or that has source evidence such as “3 days ago”, is known. | Known labels are “Posted today”, “1 day old”, or “{n} days old”, and the short date is a UTC month and day. | Otherwise the card and detail page say “Date unknown”. | An unparseable date used only by formatPostedDate reads “Fresh”.

user_story: As a visitor, I want expired and confirmed-dead listings left off the board, the map, the directory, and the API so I do not apply to them.
expected_behavior: A job is inactive when staleAfter is in the past, a source freshness rule has expired, or its source URL is on the exclusion list or in JOB_EXCLUDED_SOURCE_URLS. | The board, home counts, directory, sitemap, and /api/jobs all start from active jobs. | Duplicate title, company, location, and workplace rows, and duplicate canonical apply or source URLs, collapse to one visible listing.

user_story: As a visitor, I want aggregator copies to expire sooner than direct employer posts so stale scraped listings do not linger.
expected_behavior: Adzuna jobs older than 7 days by fetchedAt or 30 days by postedAt are inactive. | SerpAPI Google Jobs older than 7 days by fetchedAt are inactive. | Other sources are not given those extra caps.

user_story: As a visitor, I want the published listings replaced on a schedule so the Updated time and the jobs move forward without a manual deploy.
expected_behavior: The Refresh job listings workflow runs daily at 11:17 UTC and can be started with workflow_dispatch. | It runs npm run jobs:refresh, verifies the production build, and commits src/data/jobs.json back to main when listings change. | A Vercel deploy then republishes the static feed. | Visitors do not call provider APIs. They read the committed feed.
notes: Phase 2 should not dispatch this workflow. It commits to main.

user_story: As an API consumer, I want the active listings through GET /api/jobs so my tool uses the same roles as the site.
expected_behavior: GET /api/jobs returns data, filters, and meta for active jobs. | Filters match the board contract, including q and location length 1 to 200. | page defaults to 1 and limit defaults to 20, with limit from 1 to 100. | Unknown parameters, repeated parameters, and illegal values return 400 INVALID_QUERY and do not use the public cache. | Successful responses use Access-Control-Allow-Origin * and Cache-Control public, s-maxage=300, stale-while-revalidate=3600. | OPTIONS returns 204 with the same CORS headers.

user_story: As an API consumer, I want GET /api/jobs/{id} to return one active listing or a clear not-found error.
expected_behavior: An active id returns data and meta.updatedAt with the public cache headers. | An unknown or inactive id returns 404 JOB_NOT_FOUND with message “Job listing not found.” and Cache-Control no-store. | OPTIONS returns 204.

user_story: As an API consumer, I want a docs page with the endpoints, parameters, and copyable examples so I can call the API without reading the source.
expected_behavior: The top bar “API docs” link goes to /api-docs. | The page says the API is public and read-only, documents the two routes, lists the query contract, and shows curl, PowerShell, and JavaScript examples. | Code blocks can be copied. | Links include the MCP guide, /openapi.json, and the GitHub API reference. | “Browse jobs” is the broken /#open-roles link in JOB-11.
notes: The page itself renders. Its Browse jobs link is tracked as JOB-11.

user_story: As an API consumer, I want an OpenAPI document so I can generate a client from the same contract as the route.
expected_behavior: public/openapi.json is served at /openapi.json. | The API docs page links to it. | npm run docs:api regenerates it from the jobs API contract.

user_story: As a PowerShell user, I want Get-EndpointJob to query the public API so I can filter roles from a shell.
expected_behavior: The footer PowerShell link opens the module README on GitHub in a new tab with rel noopener noreferrer. | The module installs as EndpointJobs and calls the public API with no Endpoint Jobs credential. | Get-EndpointJob supports limit, page, tool, platform, workplace, sponsorship, leadership, salary shown, freshness, minimum salary, and lookup by id. | API failures are terminating errors with the HTTP status and error code.
notes: The module is a client of API-01. It is not a site login.

user_story: As an assistant user, I want search_jobs, get_job, and get_filter_options so the assistant can search the same active feed.
expected_behavior: POST /api/mcp exposes three read-only tools. | search_jobs uses the jobs API contract and returns summaries. | get_job returns one active job, or JOB_NOT_FOUND when the id is missing or inactive. | get_filter_options returns the search schema and feed updatedAt. | The server instructions say listing text is untrusted and that a missing salary or sponsorship must not be invented. | No API key is required.

user_story: As a person connecting an assistant, I want a setup page with the server URL and client steps so I can connect without reading the route.

user_story: As a visitor, I want to start Google or GitHub sign-in from the page so I can create an account without a password on this site.

user_story: As a person returning from Google or GitHub, I want the callback to finish sign-in and send me back to the page I started from.

user_story: As a signed-in user, I want Sign out to end this site’s session and return me to the home page.
expected_behavior: The account menu posts to /auth/sign-out. | A same-site post signs out with local scope and redirects 303 to / on the request origin. | The next parameter is ignored, including an external URL. | If the revoke call fails, sb-*-auth-token cookies from the request are expired with Path=/, SameSite=Lax, and not HttpOnly. | Cookie names with control characters are not copied into Set-Cookie.

user_story: As a visitor, I want the post-login redirect to stay on this site so a crafted next parameter cannot send me elsewhere.

notes: The hosted project’s redirect allow list is dashboard configuration. The local file documents the pattern the code depends on.

user_story: As a signed-in user, I want a cross-site page to be unable to sign me out so another site cannot clear my session.
